hypothesis: Question: on development patients never seen in training, does any regularized voice-based model transfer better than a constant or a demographics-only predictor, and is the reference models' failure explained by row-level overfitting to patient identity? Prior evidence (development, patient-held-out): the constant median reference scored loss 8.379 / patient-MAE 7.427, standardized Ridge(alpha 10) 8.523 / 7.490 and HGB(250 it.) 10.465 / 8.909. Both fitted references lose to the median, which is consistent with models learning patient-specific offsets that do not transfer, but a single development split of 7 patients cannot distinguish 'voice carries no transferable signal' from 'the two reference fits were under-regularized'. This program fits, inside fit_predict using only train data, 13 candidates (median, mean, age+sex linear, age+sex+test_time linear, standardized Ridge alpha 10/100/1000 with and without log transform of positively skewed voice measures, voice-only log Ridge, shallow strongly regularized HGB on all and on voice-only columns) and scores each by 7-fold GroupKFold over the 28 train patients (RMSE and equal-patient MAE) plus a shuffled 5-fold row-level KFold for contrast. It selects the lowest patient-held-out CV RMSE, refits on all train rows, predicts development, and clips to the train y range. Contrasting expected outcomes before execution: (A) if voice features carry no transferable signal, internal patient-CV will rank median/mean/demographic models on top, the development loss will be near 8.38, and row-CV RMSE will be far lower than group-CV RMSE for the flexible models (quantifying within-patient leakage); (B) if a heavily regularized or log-transformed voice model transfers, it will win the internal patient-CV and development loss should fall below 8.38 without patient-MAE worsening. Either outcome is informative: (A) redirects later rounds toward patient-level normalization/relative features; (B) identifies which regularization/transform is worth refining. Findings report all candidate CV scores, the selected candidate, log-transformed columns, and an explicit fallback flag (train median) if the pipeline fails. No transductive use of evaluation inputs beyond prediction. Exploratory, unverified rationale; a 7-patient development set is a small group-level sample.
